$comment: ★★ A LINKED OBJECT'S `/ENTRY:` IS A REFERENCE THE ARCHIVE SEARCH ANSWERS (P69 send-back 5, review-xa4 MINOR 3; D-LK-COFF-READER-SKIPPED-EVERY-LINKER-DIRECTIVE). The object NAMED to the link is cl's build of `#pragma comment(linker, "/ENTRY:dss_archived_entry") int dss_entry_ref_marker(void) { return 3; }`: it states the image's entry and does NOT define it. Only the archive's one member does -- `int dss_archived_entry(void) { return 42; }` -- and nothing else of the link refers to it. ✔MEASURED 2026-10-08 (the same main.c built by cl; link.exe 14.44.35228 and lld-link 19.1.5): both pull the member for the entry's name alone, the process starts there with no C runtime startup, and exits 42; WITHOUT the archive both refuse the name as unresolved (link.exe LNK2001, lld-link 'undefined symbol: dss_archived_entry'), and the command line's `/ENTRY:` behaves the same. A DSS link takes that answer: an entry that an object named to the link states and does not define is a REQUIRED reference of that object (`linker::requireEntryReference`), which the archive search answers as it answers an `/INCLUDE:` or an `/EXPORT:`; one nothing defines is refused by name. This `main` is the witness that the startup never ran: it would exit 7. (A member the archive search ITSELF pulls names no entry -- `examples/c/pe_foreign_directive_entry_from_an_archive_member_warned` -- so the stating object here is named to the link.) The `release` arm pins that optimizing the DSS half changes nothing: the image never runs it.

prebuiltLibraries.$comment: The bare object that STATES the entry. Its source, with the commands that rebuild it, is `tests/link/data/pe_directive_entry_reference_x86_64_pe.source.c` (cl 19.44.35228 `/c /O2 /MD /GS- /experimental:deterministic /pathmap:`; md5 a12aeb09b00410b879bc390e2f43579e). A relocatable object named to the link is an OBJECT INPUT, linked eagerly, as link.exe links one named on its command line. The witness is the directive itself.

The archive whose one member DEFINES the entry. Its source, with the commands that rebuild it, is `tests/link/data/libpe_directive_entry_definition_x86_64_pe.source.c` (the same cl build + llvm-ar 19.1.5 `rcs --format=gnu`; member md5 7dfcc67fa7cd1f36c1cc8b4623421527, archive md5 e72223602d36f58109d507eaa84502b7). The witness is the entry's own name: an archive that does not define it cannot pass.
